title: Early vs Routine Oral Nutritional Supplementation During Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial
setting: Nutrition support during definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy
design: Multicentre, open-label, randomized 1:1 clinical trial; six Chinese tertiary centres
population: Adults 18–70 years with stage II–IVA NPC, planned CCRT and baseline PG-SGA 0–8; FAS n=216 (107 vs 109).
intervention: Ensure 55.8 g three times daily from CCRT start plus nutrition counselling.
comparator: Routine ONS only after oral intake <60% of estimated requirements for three consecutive days, plus counselling.
primary_endpoint: >5% body-weight loss from baseline to CCRT completion

key_results.qol: No significant between-group difference in EORTC QLQ-C30 or RT interruptions in the accessible conference report.

data_provenance: Numerical results and ONS dose from ESMO 2025 LBA103 (DOI 10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.120). JAMA Oncology title/DOI/PMID metadata verified; full JAMA text not mined due explicit publisher restriction on AI text/data mining.
summary: Proactive ONS from the start of CCRT reduced >5% weight loss and grade ≥3 RIOM in the conference-report FAS; NNT 6 at CCRT completion for each endpoint.
clinical_interpretation: Supports early dietitian-led nutrition support in selected well-nourished NPC patients starting CCRT; does not establish a survival benefit or replace individualized escalation to enteral feeding.
limitations: Short-term outcomes only; no mature survival endpoint.
Six Chinese centres; generalizability needs confirmation.
Conference-report numerical data used because the peer-reviewed article full text restricts AI text/data mining.
QoL domain scores and detailed grade 3–5 AE tables were not available in the accessible conference abstract.
nccn_provenance: not verified — current full NCCN Head and Neck guideline/reference list inaccessible; NCCN Insights v2.2025 is limited scope and not a complete guideline.

archive_record.title: Early versus routine oral nutritional supplementation during concurrent chemoradiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a randomized clinical trial
archive_record.setting: Nutritional intervention during definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy
archive_record.population: Adults with stage II–IVA nasopharyngeal carcinoma receiving concurrent chemoradiotherapy; full analysis set 216 (107 early ONS; 109 routine ONS).
archive_record.summary: The accessible ESMO 2025 conference report and JAMA Oncology publication record support lower >5% weight loss at CCRT completion with early ONS (69.8% vs 88.8%; absolute difference 19.0 percentage points; NNT 6) and lower grade ≥3 radiation-induced oral mucositis (10.9% vs 28.0%; difference 17.1 points; NNT 6). Survival benefit is not established.
archive_record.criticalReview: The evidence supports a short-term nutritional-support strategy, not a survival claim. The batch page uses the peer-reviewed JAMA Oncology DOI and registry; full JAMA text and longer-term outcomes remain to be checked.
